288 | /* A layout used for pages where all (visible) values are the same scalar value.
289 |  *
290 |  * This generalizes the prior AllNullLayout semantics for file_version >= 2.2.
291 |  *
292 |  * There may be buffers of repetition and definition information if required in order
293 |  * to interpret what kind of nulls are present / which items are visible.
294 |  */
295 | message ConstantLayout {
296 |   // The meaning of each repdef layer, used to interpret repdef buffers correctly
297 |   repeated RepDefLayer layers = 5;
298 | 
299 |   /* Inline fixed-width scalar value bytes.
300 |    *
301 |    * This MUST only be used for types where a single non-null element is represented by a single
302 |    * fixed-width Arrow value buffer (i.e. no offsets buffer, no child data).
303 |    *
304 |    * Constraints:
305 |    * - MUST be absent for an all-null page
306 |    * - MUST be <= 32 bytes if present
307 |    */
308 |   optional bytes inline_value = 6;
309 |

12 | /* A transaction represents the changes to a dataset.
13 |  *
14 |  * This has two purposes:
15 |  * 1. When retrying a commit, the transaction can be used to re-build an updated
16 |  *    manifest.
17 |  * 2. When there's a conflict, this can be used to determine whether the other
18 |  *    transaction is compatible with this one.
19 |  */
20 | message Transaction {
21 |   /* The version of the dataset this transaction was built from.
22 |    *
23 |    * For example, for a delete transaction this means the version of the dataset
24 |    * that was read from while evaluating the deletion predicate.
25 |    */
26 |   uint64 read_version = 1;
27 | 
28 |   // The UUID that unique identifies a transaction.
29 |   string uuid = 2;
30 | 
31 |   // Optional version tag.
32 |   string tag = 3;
33 | 
34 |   /* Optional properties for the transaction
35 |    * __lance_commit_message is a reserved key
36 |    */
37 |   map<string, string> transaction_properties = 4;

97 |  * ## Data Pages
98 |  *
99 |  * A lot of flexibility is provided in how data is stored.  A page's buffers do
100 |  * not strictly need to be contiguous on the disk.  However, it is recommended
101 |  * that buffers within a page be grouped together for best performance.
102 |  *
103 |  * Data pages should be large.  The only time a page should be written to disk
104 |  * is when the writer needs to flush the page to disk because it has accumulated
105 |  * too much data.  Pages are not read in sequential order and if pages are too
106 |  * small then the seek overhead (or request overhead) will be problematic.  We
107 |  * generally advise that pages be at least 8MB or larger.
108 |  *
109 |  * ## Encodings
110 |  *
111 |  * Specific encodings are not part of this minimal format.  They are provided
112 |  * by extensions. Readers and writers should be designed so that encodings can
113 |  * be easily added and removed. Ideally, they should allow for this without
114 |  * requiring recompilation through some kind of plugin system.
115 |  */
